data.title: General Health Test
data.shortDescription: A broad home blood test covering up to 24 biomarkers across eight areas of health — heart, diabetes, liver, kidney, thyroid, iron, nutrition and muscle. Collected from your upper arm, no finger-pricking. Provided and analysed by Randox, a UKAS-accredited laboratory.
data.sampleType: Blood — QuickDraw upper-arm collection kit (no finger-pricking)
data.resultsTimeline: 2–3 working days from arrival at the lab
data.detailIntro: The General Health Test is a single home blood test that gives you a wide baseline picture of how your body is working. One sample, collected from your upper arm with the QuickDraw device supplied in the kit, covers up to 24 biomarkers grouped into eight areas of health. Post it back to the Randox laboratory in the freepost envelope included. Your results are delivered to you directly by Randox. If you would like them explained, you can book an optional follow-up consultation with an IMC-registered Global Health doctor from €45.
whatThisTestCovers: Heart health: Total Cholesterol, HDL Cholesterol, HDL Percentage, LDL Cholesterol, Non-HDL Cholesterol, Total Cholesterol / HDL Cholesterol Ratio, Triglycerides
Liver health: Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT), Albumin, Alkaline Phosphatase (ALP), Gamma-Glutamyltransferase (GGT)
Thyroid health: Thyroid Stimulating Hormone (TSH), Free Thyroxine (FT4), Free Tri-iodothyronine (FT3)
Iron status: Iron, Total Iron Binding Capacity (TIBC), Transferrin Saturation
Nutritional health: Vitamin B12, Vitamin D
whyGetTested: A general baseline check when you have no specific symptoms
Fatigue, low energy, or feeling generally run down
Family history of high cholesterol, diabetes, or thyroid problems
Checking the effect of a change in diet, training, or lifestyle
You would rather not take time off to attend a clinic

extraSections.body:
Order your kit
It is posted to your address with everything you need in the box — collection device, instructions and a prepaid return envelope.

Collect your sample
Place the QuickDraw device on your upper arm and follow the instructions. No finger-pricking, and the collection itself takes a few minutes.

Activate and post it back
Register your kit online so the laboratory can match your sample to you, then seal the prepaid envelope and drop it at any post box.

Get your results
Randox delivers them to you digitally once the laboratory has finished. A doctor consultation to talk them through is optional, from €45.
extraSections.title: How it works

extraSections.body:
Fast for 8 hours
No food for 8 hours before collecting — water is fine throughout. Eat a light meal before the fast starts and avoid alcohol.

Drink water beforehand
On the morning of collection, drink plenty of water. Being well hydrated improves circulation and makes it easier to collect a clean sample.

Pause biotin supplements
Biotin (vitamin B7), on its own or inside a multivitamin, interferes with several laboratory results. Stop 48 hours before testing — unless it was prescribed, in which case speak to your doctor first.
extraSections.title: What to know before testing

data.title: Female Hormone Test
data.shortDescription: A home blood test measuring eight hormones involved in mood, energy, metabolism and the menstrual cycle. Collected from your upper arm, no finger-pricking. Provided and analysed by Randox, a UKAS-accredited laboratory.
data.sampleType: Blood — QuickDraw upper-arm collection kit (no finger-pricking)

data.detailIntro: Hormone levels shift across the menstrual cycle and across life stages, and they influence mood, energy, weight and fertility. This kit measures eight hormones from a single sample you collect at home. Timing matters — if you have a regular cycle, collect your sample on day 3 unless advised otherwise. Your results are delivered to you directly by Randox. If you would like them explained, you can book an optional follow-up consultation with an IMC-registered Global Health doctor from €45.
whyGetTested: Irregular, absent, or unusually heavy periods
Difficulty conceiving, or planning a pregnancy
Unexplained fatigue, low mood, or weight changes

Order your kit
It is posted to your address with everything you need in the box — collection device, instructions and a prepaid return envelope.

Collect your sample
Place the QuickDraw device on your upper arm and follow the instructions. No finger-pricking, and the collection itself takes a few minutes.

Get your results

extraSections.title: How it works

extraSections.body:
Time it to your cycle
Collect your sample two to five days after your period starts, ideally on day three.

Hormonal contraception affects this
The pill changes these results. If you have recently stopped it, wait until your cycle has settled back into its normal rhythm before testing.

Drink water beforehand
On the morning of collection, drink plenty of water. Being well hydrated improves circulation and makes it easier to collect a clean sample.

Pause biotin supplements
Biotin (vitamin B7), on its own or inside a multivitamin, interferes with several laboratory results. Stop 48 hours before testing — unless it was prescribed, in which case speak to your doctor first.

Applying HRT gel, spray or cream
Keep taking it as usual, but wear gloves to apply it and never apply it to the arm you collect from — residue on the skin contaminates the sample.
extraSections.title: What to know before testing

Testosterone follows a daily rhythm and is highest early in the day, so a later sample can read misleadingly low.

data.title: PSA (Prostate) Test
data.shortDescription: A home blood test measuring Prostate Specific Antigen (PSA), a marker used in assessing prostate health. Collected from your upper arm, no finger-pricking. Provided and analysed by Randox, a UKAS-accredited laboratory.
data.sampleType: Blood — QuickDraw upper-arm collection kit (no finger-pricking)
data.resultsTimeline: 2–3 working days from arrival at the lab
data.detailIntro: PSA is a protein produced by the prostate. A raised level can have several causes — an enlarged prostate, infection, recent exercise or ejaculation, as well as prostate cancer — so PSA is a starting point for further assessment, not a diagnosis on its own. Your results are delivered to you directly by Randox. If you would like them explained, you can book an optional follow-up consultation with an IMC-registered Global Health doctor from €45.
whyGetTested: Aged over 50, or over 45 with a family history of prostate cancer
Urinary changes — frequency, urgency, a weak stream, or getting up at night
You would like a baseline PSA reading to track over time
Following up a previous PSA result at home

extraSections.title: How it works

extraSections.body:
Rest for 48 hours first
Avoid vigorous exercise, cycling and sexual activity for 48 hours before collecting — each raises PSA temporarily and can push a normal result over the line.

After an examination or infection
Wait at least 48 hours after a digital rectal examination, and six weeks after a prostate biopsy or urinary infection.

Drink water beforehand
On the morning of collection, drink plenty of water. Being well hydrated improves circulation and makes it easier to collect a clean sample.

Interest in how your diet is shaping your gut
Rebuilding after a course of antibiotics
A broader interest in immunity and energy

extraSections.body:
Order your kit
It is posted to your address with everything you need in the box — collection device, instructions and a prepaid return envelope.

Collect your sample
Use the collection container and the step-by-step instructions provided. Everything is done at home, in your own time.

Activate and post it back
Register your kit online, then seal the prepaid packaging and post it the same day you collect.

Get your results

extraSections.title: How it works

extraSections.body:
Eat normally beforehand
An unusual diet in the days before collecting gives an unrepresentative picture of your gut.

Wait after antibiotics
If you have recently finished a course, leave at least four weeks so your microbiome has settled.

Post it the same day
Collect and send on the same day so the sample reaches the laboratory in good condition.

Irish ancestry — carrier rates here are unusually high

data.title: Genetic Coeliac Disease Test
data.shortDescription: A home DNA test screening for the HLA-DQ risk markers associated with coeliac disease, from a saliva sample. Provided and analysed by Randox, a UKAS-accredited laboratory.
data.resultsTimeline: 1–2 weeks from arrival at the lab
data.detailIntro: Almost everyone who develops coeliac disease carries an HLA-DQ risk marker, so a negative result makes coeliac disease very unlikely. A positive result does not mean you have it — many carriers never develop the condition — but it means the possibility is worth pursuing. Unlike antibody testing, this test is unaffected by whether you are currently eating gluten. Your results are delivered to you directly by Randox. If you would like them explained, you can book an optional follow-up consultation with an IMC-registered Global Health doctor from €45.

You already avoid gluten, which makes antibody testing unreliable
Unexplained iron deficiency, fatigue, or weight loss

Nothing to drink, no symptoms
This reads the genetic markers rather than your reaction to lactose, so there is no lactose drink and no waiting through symptoms.

data.detailIntro: Osteoporosis is usually silent until a bone breaks. It is a risk assessment, not a bone density scan. Your results are delivered to you directly by Randox. extraSections.body:
Order your kit
It is posted to your address with everything you need in the box — collection device, instructions and a prepaid return envelope.

Collect your sample
Clip your fingernails into the container provided. No blood, no needle — a nail clipper is the only thing you need.

Activate and post it back
Register your kit online so the laboratory can match your sample to you, then seal the prepaid envelope and drop it at any post box.

Get your results
Randox delivers them to you digitally once the laboratory has finished. A doctor consultation to talk them through is optional, from €45.
extraSections.title: How it works

extraSections.body:
Grow your nails a few days
The laboratory needs enough clipping to work with, so leave them a little longer than usual before collecting.

Remove polish and gels
Take off nail polish, gel and acrylic before clipping — coatings interfere with the protein analysis.
